slot.brief: Evaluate cos α + cos(α+d) + … + cos(α + (n−1)d) using the telescoping sine-difference formula; ask for the closed form.

verdicts.working: Using the sum-to-product identity for a cosine progression, the sum is \(\frac{\sin(nd/2)}{\sin(d/2)}\cos\left(\alpha+\frac{(n-1)d}{2}\right)\), which matches (A).

working:
$2\sin\dfrac d2\cos(\alpha+kd)=\sin\left(\alpha+(k+\dfrac12)d\right)-\sin\left(\alpha+(k-\dfrac12)d\right)$.
Summing for $k=0,\ldots,n-1$ and using the sine-difference identity gives $\displaystyle\frac{\sin\dfrac{nd}{2}}{\sin\dfrac d2}\cos\left(\alpha+\dfrac{(n-1)d}{2}\right)$.
